newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African opposition parties slam health bills.
newsitem.headline: S.African opposition parties slam health bills.

text.p: Opposition parties on Monday slammed efforts by the African National Congress to ram a controversial health bill through parliament.
They refused to take part in discussions in the parliamentary portfolio committee on health on the Pharmacy Amendment Bill, which has been considerably amended since it was gazetted.

Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) health spokeswoman Ruth Rabinowitz said all parties supported the drive to try to make more and cheaper medicines available to the public, but this had to be done correctly.
A joint statement on Monday by the IFP, Democratic Party, National Party, Pan Africanist Congress and the African Christian Democratic Party condemned efforts to push the bill through parliament.
Twenty-eight organisations attended public hearing on the bill, which, among other things, aims to allow non-pharmacists to own and run pharmacies.
